questions.question: Describe the differences between General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and General Agreement on Trade in Services.
questions.solution_html:
• The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GA TT) and the General Agreement on Trade in
  • Services differ in several key aspects. GA TT, established in 1947, focuses on the promotion of
  • international trade in goods and mainly covers physical products such as manufactured items and
  • raw materials. In contrast, GA TS, introduced in 1995, deals with trade in services, including
  • sectors like banking, information technology, and tourism. While GA TT aims at reducing tariffs
  • and barriers on goods, GA TS provides a framework for liberalizing and regulating global trade in
  • services.
questions.final_answer: services.

questions.question: Explain the concept of free trade and protectionism with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Free trade is a system in which countries exchange goods and services without significant
  • restrictions such as tariffs, quotas, or import bans. It promotes open markets and allows
  • countries to specialize based on their comparative advantage. For example, under rules of the
  • World Trade Organization, many countries reduce tariffs to encourage global trade.
  • Protectionism, on the other hand, refers to government policies that restrict imports to protect
  • domestic industries from foreign competition. These measures include tariffs, quotas, subsidies
  • and import restrictions. For example, a country may impose high import duties on foreign steel
  • to protect its local steel industry.
questions.final_answer: to protect its local steel industry.

questions.question: Discuss the differences between domestic and international trade in terms of scope and operation.
questions.solution_html:
• Domestic trade refers to trade that takes place within a country, while international trade
  • occurs between different countries.
  • In domestic trade, the same currency is used, whereas international trade involves different
  • currencies.
  • Domestic trade is subject to fewer restrictions and simpler regulations, while international trade
  • requires compliance with more complex legal formalities and customs procedures.
  • Transport in domestic trade is generally easier, faster, and cheaper, whereas in international trade
  • it is more complex and costly due to long distances and logistics.
  • Finally, domestic trade involves lower risk, while international trade carries higher risk due to
  • factors such as exchange rate fluctuations and political instability.
questions.final_answer: factors such as exchange rate fluctuations and political instability.

questions.question: What is CBAM? Discuss key aspects of CBAM?
questions.solution_html:
• The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is a policy introduced by the European
  • Union to impose carbon costs on imports based on their carbon emissions.
  • Key aspects
  • • Applies to carbon-intensive products (steel, cement, etc.)
  • • Prevents “carbon leakage” (shifting production to countries with lax climate rules)
  • • Encourages cleaner production globally
  • • Importers must report emissions and may pay carbon charges
questions.final_answer: • Importers must report emissions and may pay carbon charges
